previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and gastrostomy tube dependence was admitted to the surgery service for one week of severe diffuse abdominal cramping with distension, loose stools, and one episode of clear emesis after recent gastrostomy tube change for leakage. She was evaluated with labs (including normal WBC and lactate) and abdominal imaging; abdominal radiographs were nonobstructive and CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast showed no obstruction, unchanged gastrostomy tube position in the gastric remnant, and no CT evidence of internal hernia. She was managed with observation, initial NPO status with IV hydration and antiemetics, then gradual re-trial of water and tube feeds with good tolerance, and transition to oral pain control. She remained afebrile and hemodynamically stable without signs of infection or bleeding and was discharged home ambulatory, tolerating Stage III diet and tube feeds, with instructions to avoid NSAIDs, crush pills, and follow up with her surgical team.

Discharge Disposition:
Home
 
Discharge Diagnosis:
Hypoglycemia s/p Roux-en-Y gastric bypass
S/p bypass reversal
 
Discharge Condition:
Mental Status: Clear and coherent.
Level of Consciousness: Alert and interactive.
Activity Status: Ambulatory - Independent.
 
Discharge Instructions:
Please call your surgeon or return to the emergency department 
if you develop a fever greater than 101.5, chest pain, shortness 
of breath, severe abdominal pain, pain unrelieved by your pain 
medication, severe nausea or vomiting, severe abdominal 
bloating, inability to eat or drink, foul smelling or colorful 
drainage from your incisions, redness or swelling around your 
incisions, or any other symptoms which are concerning to you.  

Diet: Stay on Stage III diet until your follow up appointment. 
Do not self advance diet, do not drink out of a straw or chew 
gum.
Resume your home medications, CRUSH ALL PILLS.  

You should continue to monitor your blood glucose closely. 
Please continue to use your continuous glucose monitor at home. 
If you find that your blood glucose is low, or you are having 
symptoms of hypoglycemia (dizziness, fast heart beat, weakness, 
change in vision), take a glucose packet prescribed to you or 
eat sugar, such as a cup of juice. If you feel you are not 
recovering or having severe symptoms (loss of consciousness), 
you should call ___ and/or go to the ED.

You will be starting some new medications:  
1. You are being discharged on medications to treat the pain  
from your operation. These medications will make you drowsy and  

impair your ability to drive a motor vehicle or operate  
machinery safely. You MUST refrain from such activities while  
taking these medications.  
2. You should begin taking a chewable complete multivitamin with 
 
minerals. No gummy vitamins.  
3. You will be taking pantoprazole liquid 40 mg twice daily for 
one  
month. This medicine prevents gastric reflux.  
4. You should take a stool softener, Colace, twice daily for  
constipation as needed, or until you resume a normal bowel  
pattern.  
5. You must not use NSAIDS (non-steroidal anti-inflammatory  
drugs) Examples are Ibuprofen, Motrin, Aleve, Nuprin and  
Naproxen. These agents will cause bleeding and ulcers in your  
digestive system.  
6. You are being given a prescription for Zofran 4mg to be taken 
every 8 hours as needed for nausea.

Activity:  
No heavy lifting of items ___ pounds for 6 weeks. You may  
resume moderate exercise at your discretion, no abdominal  
exercises.  

Wound Care:  
You may shower, no tub baths or swimming.  
If there is clear drainage from your incisions, cover with  
clean, dry gauze.  
Your staples will be removed during your follow-up appointment. 
 
Please call the doctor if you have increased pain, swelling,  
redness, or drainage from the incision sites.
